content: 1. Administer 50 mg of dapsone orally once daily, and titrate the dose up to 300 mg daily or higher to achieve the desired therapeutic effect. Once the desired effect is achieved, reduce the dose to the minimum effective dose within the range of 50–300 mg daily as soon as possible. 2. Administer 100 mg of dapsone orally once daily in combination with other antileprosy drugs. Alternatively, administer 100 mg of dapsone orally once daily with rifampin 600 mg orally once daily. 3. For prophylaxis in severely immunocompromised patients (CD4 count <100), administer 1–2 mg/kg of dapsone orally once daily, not exceeding 100 mg/day, in combination with other antileprosy agents. 4. Aluminum hydroxide decreases the level or effect of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates. If coadministration is unavoidable, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. 6. Dapsone decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 7. Calcium carbonate decreases the level or effect of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Avoid coadministration of topical dapsone with oral dapsone or antimalarial medications due to the potential for hemolytic reactions. 9. Famotidine decreases the level or effect of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 11. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases the level or effect of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Idelalisib increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 13. Ivosidenib decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. 14. Lansoprazole decreases the level or effect of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Lonafarnib increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates as per product labeling. 16. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of dapsone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. This combination increases the risk of hemolytic reactions. 17. Nefazodone increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Avoid coadministration of selinexor with dapsone due to an unspecified interaction mechanism. Patients treated with selinexor may experience neurological toxicities. Avoid taking selinexor with other medications that may cause dizziness or confusion. 19. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the level or effect of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases the level or effect of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Tucatinib increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates, where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as per product labeling. 22. Dapsone decreases the effects of the typhoid vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 23. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Apalutamide, a weak CYP2C9 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs that are CYP2C9 substrates. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if coadministration is necessary. 24. Dapsone decreases the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 25. Belzutifan decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate as per its prescribing information. 26. Dapsone and bupivacaine implant may increase the toxicity of each other through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. Local anesthetics may increase the risk of developing methemoglobinemia when concurrently exposed to drugs that also cause methemoglobinemia. 27. Cannabidiol increases the level or effect of dapsone by decreasing metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cannabidiol may inhibit CYP2C9 activity. Consider reducing the dose when using CYP2C9 substrates concomitantly. 28. Carbamazepine decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Cenobamate decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 30. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Dapsone decreases the level or effect of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 33. Crizotinib increases the level of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Dose reduction may be needed for coadministered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 34. Crofelemer increases the level of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Crofelemer may inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. 35. Dabrafenib decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 36. Deferasirox decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 37. Didanosine increases the toxicity of dapsone through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. This combination may increase the risk of nerve damage. 38. Dapsone increases the level or effect of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 39. Efavirenz decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Elagolix decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered. Consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. 41. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the level of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elvitegravir also decreases the level of dapsone by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer. 42. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Coadministration of encorafenib with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents. Use caution and monitor. 43. Enzalutamide decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Dapsone decreases the level or effect of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 46. Dapsone decreases the level or effect of estrogens (conjugated synthetic) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 47. Dapsone decreases the level or effect of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 48. Fedratinib increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 49. Iloperidone increases the level of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 50. Isoniazid increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism and by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Istradefylline increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 52. Ketoconazole increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Lenacapavir increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last SC dose of lenacapavir, which may increase the potential risk of adverse reactions of CYP3A4 substrates. 54. Letermovir increases the level of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Levoketoconazole increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 56. Lorlatinib decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor affects hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. In vitro studies suggest that lumacaftor may induce and ivacaftor may inhibit CYP2C9 substrates. 58. Dapsone decreases the level or effect of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 59. Dapsone and methotrexate may increase the risk of hematologic toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 60. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9. Use caution and monitor. Use the smallest recommended doses for substrates and monitor. 61. Mitotane decreases the level of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4; monitor when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates for possible dosage adjustments. 62. Nitisinone increases the level or effect of dapsone by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Nitisinone inhibits CYP2C9. Caution is advised if CYP2C9 substrates are coadministered, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index. 63. Peginterferon alfa-2b decreases the level of dapsone by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. When patients are administered peginterferon alpha-2b with CYP2C9 substrates, the therapeutic effect of these drugs may be altered. 64. Rifabutin decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 66. Dapsone decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. 67. Sparsentan decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Sparsentan, a CYP2C9 inducer, decreases exposure of CYP2C9 substrates and reduces efficacy related to these substrates. 68. St. John’s Wort decreases the level or effect of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
